sections.title: Cover Letter
sections.description:
Enclosed in this proposal, you will find a comprehensive overview of the recommended solution for implementing a modern phone system for your business.


This proposal outlines all the necessary details, including hardware, software, services, and optional add-ons. I’ve taken great care to break down each phase of the project—ranging from procurement to installation—along with associated costs and payment milestones. There’s a lot of information to go through, so please take your time to review everything.


After revisiting the setup, I’ve realized that this project will require a bit more time and effort than originally estimated in 2023. I’ve also opted to include business-grade hardware, as I did last time, to ensure maximum reliability. While this will add a little extra setup time, it’s a far more dependable solution in the long run. The system I’ve outlined will be well-suited to your business size and should serve you well for the next three to five years.


Here’s a quick breakdown of my recommendations

- Switch your internet provider to Exetel Business, with a 100/40 Mbps service.

- Switch your VOIP service from Telstra to Aatrox Communications, with two SIP lines.

- Install a cloud-hosted vPBX phone system to manage both internal and external communications to replace the existing Panasonic Phone System

- Replace your existing networking equipment provided by Telstra and install new network switches that can deliver power and internet to your desk phones.

- Set up an automated backup system for your vPBX, with one backup stored locally and another replicated to a cloud service.


Optional Recommendations

- Supply and install power protection hardware to safeguard your equipment against power outages or surges.


I’ve also included a Scope of Works document within this proposal to give you a clear understanding of the steps needed to implement this system. I’m confident this solution will meet your needs and deliver great value. However, if you’d like to explore other options for comparison, I completely understand and encourage you to do so to ensure you’re getting the best deal.


If you have any questions or need further clarification about any aspect of this proposal, please don’t hesitate to reach out. I’m more than happy to discuss any adjustments or address any concerns you may have with my recommendations.


Thank you for considering me for this project, again, feel free to contact me if you have any questions.

sections.title: Scope Of Works
sections.description:
This Scope of Works (SOW) outlines the objectives, deliverables, and approach for the successful execution of the project. It provides a clear framework to define responsibilities, milestones, and expected outcomes, ensuring alignment between all parties and a shared understanding of the project's scope. Please ensure you have a full understanding of what is included, as well as any exclusions, before proceeding with the project to ensure that expectations are clearly set and all requirements are met.


Objective

The objective is to transition the current Telstra Business Internet and Voice services to Exetel and Aatrox Communications. This includes implementing an on-premises 3CX vPBX phone system, upgrading network infrastructure, and ensuring all systems are configured, deployed, and operational.


Deliverables & Tasks

This section outlines the specific outputs and results that will be provided upon completion of the project. It serves to define the tangible items, services, or milestones that are expected to be delivered, ensuring that all parties have a shared understanding of what will be provided and when.


Business Internet Service & Voice Service

- Transition from Telstra to Exetel Business Internet.

- Provision and configure Exetel Business - Start Up NBN Plan (100/40 Mbps).

- Transition from Telstra Business Voice to Aatrox Communications SIP lines.

- Provision the following Aatrox services: 1x Capped SIP Line for 1 channel and hosting 1 number and 1x Pay-As-You-Go SIP Line for cost-effective call handling.

- Hosting of five (5) existing numbers: 6652 5061, 6652 7670, 6652 2592, 6658 0610 & 6651 6505.

- Configure and test all SIP lines with the 3CX phone system.


Cloud Hosted vPBX Phone System

- Deploy and configure a cloud hosted virtual private server.

- Install and configure 3CX software with proposed 4 Channel Professional License.

- Configure 3CX features, including Presence. Office 365 and Outlook integration and mobile client access for remote calls.

- Configure after-hours voicemail system; and out-of-office call re-routing.

- Preconfigure replacement deskphones and DECT system.

- Register and configure phones with 3CX system.

- Test internal calling, and system routing.

- Install devices onsite, and ensure connectivity is working.

- Overall check of system to ensure full functionality prior to number porting.


Network Infrastructure

- Pre-configure new hardware, which includes the Unifi Express, and Network Switching.

- Replace existing Telstra Business router and switches with Ubiquiti network hardware:

- Replace all outdated cabling with CAT6 Ethernet cables.

- Recable, clean and reorganize network connections for easier maintenance.

- Setup remote access capabilities for both my use to maintain systems, and for your use to access the network from anywhere.


Disposing Of Old Equipment

- Following cutover to new services, I am also happy to dispose of the old phone system equipment.


Exclusions

The following items are not included in this scope:

- Existing Telstra contract cancellation fees (please check with Telstra Business on what may occur).

- Costs associated with unforeseen structural changes for equipment installation.

- Advanced customizations beyond the listed 3CX features.


Assumptions

Existing systems (hardware and infrastructure) are in operational condition and can be repurposed.

Full access to the site and existing network setup will be provided.


Timeline

Based on current hardware procurement lead-times, and number porting timeframes, the end-to-end project timeline is 2-3 weeks following approval. This can and may be affected by hardware procurement and third-party turn around.

milestones.title: Phase 1 - Project Approval Deposit & Hardware Procurement
milestones.description:
This phase includes obtaining formal approval, confirming project scope, budget, and timelines. Once the project is approved, and a deposit invoice has been paid, the necessary hardware, such as phones, systems, and networking equipment, will be ordered and procured. The hardware procurement invoice will cover the cost of the equipment, any associated licenses, shipping, and handling fees. To ensure timely procurement of all required components is essential to avoid delays and guarantee that the system is ready for configuration and installation. This invoice will be issued upon confirmation and approval of this proposal.


ETC: Immediately following clearance of payment

Estimated Invoice Date: Immediately following written approval

milestones.title: Phase 2 - Completion of Workshop Preconfiguration
milestones.description:
During this phase, the phone system will be preconfigured in a workshop or lab environment. This includes setting up the PBX system, networking equipment, configuring phones, programming extensions, and ensuring compatibility with existing networks. Invoices for this phase may include labor costs for pre-configuration, software installations, and any additional tools or licensing fees for the system. Preconfiguration ensures that the system is ready for deployment and minimizes the risk of issues during the physical installation. All configurations will be tested before moving to the next phase.


ETC: 1 to 2 weeks following hardware procurement

Estimated Invoice Date: 2-3 days after all hardware arrives and has been configured.

milestones.title: Phase 3 - Completion of Physical Installation
milestones.description:
This phase marks the on-site installation of the phone system hardware, including the physical setup of phones, wiring, enclosures, and systems, along with connecting to the company’s network. The phone system will be fully integrated with the organization’s infrastructure. In preparation for cutover, I will ensure that the system is correctly installed and operational, and final adjustments will be made based on the physical environment and requirements.


ETC: Installation Date TBC

Estimated Invoice Date: Nill Invoice

milestones.title: Phase 4 - Completion of System Cutover & Project Finalisation
milestones.description:
The final phase involves the cutover to the new phone system, which includes transferring phone numbers, configuring voicemail, and ensuring all internal and external communication channels are working properly. System testing, user training, and troubleshooting will occur to confirm full functionality. The final invoice for this phase will include any remaining installation labor, system testing, training costs, and project management fees. Once all services are tested and confirmed as working, the project will be finalized. Documentation will be provided, and ongoing support options will be discussed. The project is officially completed when the final invoice is settled, and the system is fully operational.


ETC: Installation Date TBC

Estimated Invoice Date: Immediately following cutover to new system
